sections.title: Structure and Expressiveness of Hungarian Twin-Words
sections.content: Hungarian possesses a rich inventory of twin-words (ikerszók), created through playful reduplication, rhyming stems, and ablaut patterns. In spoken Hungarian and colorful informal writing, these words bring immediate vividness to descriptions, evoking clutter, confusion, gossip, or sensory detail with playful irony.

sections.title: Rhyming Compounds: Gizgaz, Limlom, and Hercehurca
sections.content: Rhyming twin-words join two phonetically parallel elements where either both are meaningful or one acts as an echo word. Fixed rhyming noun compounds like 'gizgaz' (weeds/scrub), 'limlom' (useless clutter), 'hercehurca' (tedious bureaucratic hassle), and 'terefere' (idle chit-chat) typically inflect only on their second element (e.g. sok limlomot gyűjtött össze).

sections.title: Frequent Rhyming Twin-Words in Living Hungarian
rows: A padlás tele van mindenféle limlommal.
The attic is full of all sorts of odds and ends.
Nem akartunk belemenni a hivatalos hercehurcába.
We did not want to get involved in the tedious bureaucratic hassle.
A kert végében csak a gaz és a gizgaz burjánzott.
At the end of the garden, only weeds and wild scrub proliferated.
Egy kellemes kávé melletti terefere mindig felvidít.
A pleasant chit-chat over a coffee always cheers one up.

items.spanish: A régi ifjúsági klub padlásán sok elfeledett limlom hevert az évtizedek alatt.
items.english: In the attic of the old youth club, a lot of forgotten junk lay over the decades.

items.spanish: Hosszas bürokratikus hercehurca után engedélyezték végül a koncert megtartását.
items.english: After lengthy bureaucratic hassle, they finally permitted the concert to be held.

items.spanish: A lányok órákon át tereferéltek a próbaterem előtt az új lemezekről.
items.english: The girls chatted for hours in front of the rehearsal room about the new records.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: Distinguish separable twin-words (like izeg-mozog, where both components can inflect: izgett-mozgott) from fused rhyming nouns (like limlom, hercehurca, gizgaz), which inflect only at the very end: limlomok, hercehurcát.
